Object.Name: AppMessaging
Object.Description1: Provides application messaging and configuration between an LwM2M Server and applications on an LwM2M Client. Separate Resources carry Server to Client and Client to Server messages. Each Object Instance identifies an application through Resource 4050 (AppID). Resource 4051 links to the corresponding Software Management /9 instance.

Item.Name: AppID
Item.Description: A unique local-scope identifier for distinguishing edge applications within a specific deployment environment.

Item.Name: Software Instance
Item.Description: Object link to the corresponding LwM2M Software Management /9 instance for the installed application. Together with AppID, this link correlates the logical application identity with the specific installed software instance on this endpoint.

Item.Name: Server Message
Item.Description: Write-only payload for a Server to Client message. Implementations that support /3600 SHALL support this resource as the inbound application-message write surface, subject to authorization and routing policy.

Item.Name: Client Message
Item.Description: Readable payload for a Client to Server message or the current app-message slot. The resource may be unavailable when no message is pending; durable history is provided by Object /20.

Item.Name: Message Priority
Item.Description:
Indicates the app-message priority for this app-scoped messaging instance.
For values 1 through 4, lower numeric values represent higher delivery priority. Value 0 (Unspecified) MUST NOT be interpreted as a higher priority than Urgent. Edge platforms SHOULD use this value when ordering, scheduling, throttling, or selecting messages for delivery. Platforms MAY also map these priority values to local transport, queueing, or QoS policy mechanisms, including implementation-specific QoS codepoints or classes where available.
Platforms SHOULD use this priority order when competing messages are otherwise eligible for delivery.
0: Unspecified 1: Urgent - highest priority; send immediately when possible 2: Immediate - high priority; send as soon as possible 3: BestEffort - normal priority; send when resources are available 4: Latest - lowest priority; retain/send only the latest applicable message 5-100: Reserved for future GEISA use. 101-254: Reserved for proprietary use. 255: Reserved.

Item.Name: Message Type
Item.Description: Classifies the app-message payload carried by this app-scoped messaging instance. Applies to both Client Message (Resource 1) and Server Message (Resource 0). Not all types apply in both directions. 0: UNSPECIFIED - Message type is not specified or not yet classified. 1: CONFIG - App-facing desired or effective configuration state. 2: COMMAND - Action request to perform work now or soon. 3: COMMAND_RESULT - Result of a COMMAND execution, distinct from transport-level response acceptance. 4: STATUS - Current state, lifecycle, readiness, mode, or policy/quota state. 5: EVENT - Operationally meaningful occurrence worth recording or routing. 6: ALARM - Actionable, high-severity, security, safety, or policy condition requiring prompt attention or special handling. 7: APP_DATA - Supplemental application-specific data that intentionally does not fit CONFIG, COMMAND, STATUS, EVENT, ALARM, COMMAND_RESULT, or TELEMETRY. 8: TELEMETRY - Measurement-oriented numeric or structured observations, usually time-series, snapshot, interval, or resource metrics. 9-100: Reserved for future GEISA use. 101-254: Reserved for Proprietary use.

Item.Name: Message TTL
Item.Description: Requested or default app-message time-to-live for this app-scoped messaging instance, in seconds. A value of 0 indicates no message-specific TTL and allows the platform or EMS to apply default policy. This resource is not event-log retention. Expired messages SHALL NOT be delivered as current app messages, though expiration may be recorded through event or log mechanisms where appropriate.

Item.Name: Content Type
Item.Description: Media type for the app-message payload encoding, such as application/json, application/cbor, application/octet-stream, application/protobuf, or a GEISA or vendor-specific media type. This allows routing and interpretation without assuming all message payloads are opaque. This resource does not expose payload history. application/octet-stream may be used for opaque payloads.

Item.Name: Request ID
Item.Description: Sender-assigned identifier for the application message. The Platform and EMS preserve it across application-message transport. It applies to both Client to Server and Server to Client messages.

Item.Name: Message Timestamp
Item.Description: UTC epoch time in microseconds when the sender created the application message. This is the origin timestamp, not Platform receipt time or EMS receipt time. It applies to both Client to Server and Server to Client messages.
